Traditionally it accompanied singing, and it also has instrumental pieces; it was once popular among samurai, literati and monks, and today very few people play it. The unbroken line of transmission is the Seikyodo Ichigenkin, whose present head, Issui Minegishi, performs in North America, Europe and Asia.
